analysis:
Examined head text of ClusterService.swift lines 1-910. The changed ranges fall mostly beyond the visible lines: line 107-108 adds an `updateWaitLine` private var (benign, guarded by `lock`), and the other changes at 943, 974-984 and 989 are outside the supplied excerpt (the patch excerpt is truncated). The visible range shows no security-relevant change.

Pre-existing behavior reviewed, not new: the cluster control channel is keyed by the pairing edge secret. `command()` enforces `followsPeer` for serve/stop/approval and checks claim supersession. `receive()` applies the leader's setup only after `ClusterConsoleObserver.approve`. The local API token goes only to our own solo server (`soloReadiness`). `stopLeftover` signals only a PID whose start time matches. The lock files are created with mode 0600 in a private directory. None of this was changed by the PR.

Change worth noting: the new `pairUpdate` status field reads update progress via `ClusterServiceAgent.updateProgressPath`. Its implementation is not supplied. The new `oneBuild` gate delays re-setup until both Macs report the same runtime binary SHA. The gate's logic is not visible; it affects availability only, and the peer-reported hash is already trusted at the pairing level. Open questions for integration: (1) whether `ClusterPairUpdate.readProgress` parses the progress file defensively (size bound, owner-only file); (2) whether `oneBuild` could leave a pair indefinitely stalled. Neither was verifiable from the supplied evidence, so no finding is raised. Related threat IDs: T-043 and TB-003 (update and rollback authority), which only apply if the next pass finds a change there.
